clue.text: Men captured in error if pawns so arranged

indicators.note: pieces arranged are set out in a new order, so these letters are put into a fresh sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chess player muses that pawns set up this way would be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the fodder is the fourteen letters of 'error if pawns so', and 'arranged' at the end tells you to shuffle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers taken by the enemy during a conflict are held as captives until released or exchanged.

clue.text: Examining bird admitted by doctor turning up

indicators.note: something admitted by another is let inside it, so the bird goes within the doctor's letters
in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
the robin is a familiar garden bird

explanation.surface: A doctor studies a bird that has been brought into the surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turning up' means reading from the bottom, so the doctor's letters run backwards before taking in the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Probing a matter means investigating it closely, a synonym of scrutinising it.

clue.text: I am tentative about a theatrical opening that's unrehearsed

parts.note: contracted to I'M

indicators.note: one thing about another surrounds it, so the tentative word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a provisional arrangement is tentative, not yet final

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: supplies its first letter T

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to nerves about a first night that has had no rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatrical opening' looks like a first night, but 'opening' just takes the first letter of 'theatrical'.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvisational performance is made up on the spot, without any rehearsal beforehand.

clue.text: Married with ring that's outstanding

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
to wed is to marry, so married gives wed

explanation.surface: A newly married couple still has payments left on the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still unpaid, and so is money owed.

clue.text: Avoid legal action when held up in station

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means the letters are lifted so they read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to avoid legal action is to not sue

explanation.surface: Someone delayed at a railway terminus decides not to take the rail company to court.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT SUE read upwards gives the answer. EUSTON is a major London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a mainline railway terminus in London, an example of a train station.

clue.text: Second highest mountain is extremely hard

parts.note: Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: A claim that the world's second highest peak is the toughest climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second highest' reads as one phrase (K2), but 'Second' gives just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest is the superlative of severe, harshest or most demanding.

clue.text: It could produce a small fear mistakenly

definitions.text: It could produce a small fear mistakenly

indicators.note: letters taken mistakenly are put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning bell that goes off for no reason causes a brief scare.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning raised in error, which briefly frightens people for nothing.

clue.text: Deem a democracy incomplete if this liberty is destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an incomplete word loses its last letter, here the final Y

parts.note: supplies DEMOCRAC once its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A warning that a democracy would be diminished if this liberty were destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' docks the last letter of 'democracy' before everything from 'Deem' to 'if' is shuffled by 'destroyed'; the definition is the 'liberty' that the clue imagines destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars' right to teach and research without interference is a liberty prized in universities.

clue.text: Semi-precious stone mounted for group of high-fliers

parts.note: jet is a black gem made from fossilised wood
a gem mounted in a ring is set

explanation.surface: A jeweller fits a gem for a rich clientele.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy socialites who fly around the world, punningly high-fliers.

clue.text: Crush page inside old papers

indicators.note: the page goes inside the papers' letters

parts.note: newspapers collectively are the press

explanation.surface: A page tucked into old newspapers gets flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to subjugate or keep down by force, just as one might crush a revolt.

clue.text: Hamlet revealing evil without delay

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the evil word goes round the delay
revealing suggests the letters of evil are uncovered in a fresh arrangement, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A performance of Shakespeare's Hamlet promptly exposes villainy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests the play, but here it is a small settlement. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the reworked letters go round the delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small settlement, a little smaller than a typical village.

clue.text: One old-fashioned hero

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped or made anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three letters to be reworked

explanation.surface: Someone's idol is an old-fashioned kind of hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one adjective, but it splits: 'old' is the fodder and 'fashioned' the signal to rework it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person greatly admired and looked up to, much like a hero.

clue.text: Crude quality of lessons reported to head

indicators.note: reported means as heard spoken, so the lessons word gives a word sounding the same

parts.note: a series of lessons is a course
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: Someone's crude behaviour in lessons is reported to the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a head teacher; it is a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarseness is vulgarity or roughness of manner, the state of being crude.

clue.text: Fragrant flower mother grew after request

indicators.note: the grew word comes after the request word in the answer

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
to ask is to request
rose means increased or grew

explanation.surface: Mother cultivated a scented bloom when someone asked her to.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask rose is an old, highly scented variety used for attar of roses.

clue.text: Short screw secures it for instrument

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it inside, so the shortened word goes round it
a short word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison guard
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to tighten a stubby screw to fix something onto a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screw' looks like a fastener; it is prison slang for a warder, GUARD, which loses D and holds IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is a stringed musical instrument played by plucking or strumming.

clue.text: David's son taken in by fortune-teller

definitions.note: read as David is: King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms

indicators.note: a son taken in is held inside the fortune-teller's letters

parts.note: a palmist reads fortunes from the lines of the hand
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: David's boy is fooled by a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'David's son' reads as Solomon, but 'David's' is the definition (David is) and 'son' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms, so he is the Psalmist of the Bible.

clue.text: Not, after disappearance of old, island seen in maps

definitions.text: Not, after disappearance of old, island seen in maps

indicators.note: letters seen in a word are placed inside it

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: the old letter disappears, leaving the rest of the word

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: A legendary island is no longer on maps since it vanished long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the legendary island, lost of old and no longer seen on any map.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island of Plato's tale, said to have sunk into the sea long ago.

clue.text: Even when rebuffed accepting a role in social gathering

indicators.note: a word accepting another takes it inside
rebuffed means pushed back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: even as in 'even now' means yet
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: Someone even turned down takes on a role at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' is not about numbers but means 'yet', as in 'even now'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is an afternoon social occasion where guests meet over tea and cakes.

clue.text: Small, and a bit tight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tiny, an informal British word
second meaning: slightly drunk, tight being slang for drunk

explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' could be a snug fit; here it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means both very little and mildly tipsy after a drink or two.

clue.text: Advantage it bestowed on chairperson?

indicators.note: the word it is placed onto the end of the chairperson word

parts.note: a professor holds a university chair, so a prof is a chairperson in a punning sense
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what benefit is conferred on the person chairing a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a chairperson here is a professor holding a chair, not someone running a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is gain or benefit from something, an advantage gained.

clue.text: Highly controlled spinner joining county

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A tightly managed bowler links up with a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket spin bowler; it is the toy. Down is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-down organisation is directed from the top of the hierarchy, controlled from on high.

clue.text: Recalled country I ran without a break since 1935

definitions.text: Recalled country I ran without a break since 1935

parts.words: Recalled country I ran without a break since 1935
parts.note: a country remembered by an old name; run together, 'I ran' is the name it has used since 1935

explanation.walkthrough: 'I ran without a break' looks like a boast of a long run, but joined without a gap it spells the modern name of the country, adopted in 1935.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the name used internationally for Iran until the government asked for the change in 1935.

clue.text: Poet's order to horse that's unenforceable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John ..., English poet and playwright (Poet's read as poet is)
second meaning: from the saying that you can lead a horse to water but cannot make it drink

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says you can lead a horse to water but you can't make it drink, so this command can never be enforced.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Georgian poet John Drinkwater doubles as a command to a thirsty animal.

clue.text: Spring this year's a little longer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ... year has an extra day, 29 February

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season but is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap is a jump, and a leap year runs to 366 days instead of 365.

clue.text: Club that's used to deter attackers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a heavy spiked staff used as a weapon
second meaning: a brand of irritant spray used for self-defence

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are weapons: a medieval club and a modern self-defence spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy ceremonial or battle club, and Mace is a tear-gas spray carried for protection.

clue.text: Way to resume play with part of actor's speech removed

parts.note: an actor's script is made up of lines
something removed has been taken out

explanation.surface: A director cuts a line from an actor's speech so the play can go on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests the theatre; it is rugby, where a line-out restarts the game after the ball goes into touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union, a line-out restarts the game after the ball leaves the field at the side.

clue.text: Unspecified person also interrupting moderate

indicators.note: the also word interrupts by sitting in the middle of the moderate word

parts.note: so-so means middling or moderate
and means in addition, also

explanation.surface: Someone else also cuts in on a mild-mannered speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so stands for a person whose name is not given, a placeholder for anyone.

clue.text: Disruption of trade meant less for veteran politician

indicators.note: disruption breaks up the order of things, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old political hand warns that strikes meant less business.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder statesman is a senior, experienced politician whose advice is respected.
